outcomes.text: Calculate triangle angles from the slopes of its sides.
Apply coordinate geometry to aviation, navigation, landscaping, map reading, longitude, and latitude problems.

topics.title: Area and Volume of Similar Figures

subtopics.title: Area and Volume of Similar Figures

outcomes.text: Convert area and volume measurements between standard square and cubic units manually and with suitable apps.
Recognize when polygons are similar.
Determine the relationship between the areas of similar figures.
Determine the relationship between the volumes of similar solids.
Solve problems involving areas of similar figures and volumes of cubes, cuboids, cones, cylinders, and spheres.
Construct triangles using specified sides and angles with a ruler, protractor, and compasses.
Construct triangle bisectors, perpendicular bisectors, medians, and altitudes, then verify their concurrency.
Identify angles in standard position and express them in degrees.
Determine trigonometric ratios for acute angles in right triangles.
Use Pythagoras’ theorem and trigonometric ratios to find unknown sides and angles in right triangles.
Solve two-dimensional real-life problems involving angles of elevation and depression.
Create grouped frequency tables, histograms with equal or unequal intervals, and frequency polygons manually or with apps.
Calculate grouped-data mean by the direct method, median, and mode manually or with spreadsheet software.
Use mean, median, and mode to solve real-life problems involving given data.
Calculate the probabilities of a single event and its complement.
Calculate relative and expected frequencies as probability estimates.
Solve real-life problems using probability, relative frequencies, and expected frequencies.
Locate the centre of a given circle.
Construct a circle through three given noncollinear points.
Complete a circle from part of its circumference, with or without locating its centre.
Construct a tangent to a circle from a point on its circumference or outside it.
Construct two tangents to a circle that meet at a specified angle.
Apply circle construction principles to real-world problems involving tracks, parks, Ferris wheels, and mechanical models.
Solve triangles using the sine rule and cosine rule.
Calculate triangle areas using appropriate formulas.
Apply trigonometry to real-world problems involving games, flight engineering, navigation, and sound waves.
Create cumulative frequency tables, polygons, and curves manually or with suitable apps.
Interpret the median, quartiles, and interquartile range from a cumulative frequency curve.
Calculate range, standard deviation, and variance for grouped data manually or with suitable apps.
Compare two data sets using their means and standard deviations.
Use measures of dispersion to solve real-life problems involving consistency and variability.
Calculate combined-event probabilities using sample-space, possibility, and tree diagrams where appropriate.
Apply the addition rule to solve probability problems involving mutually exclusive events.
